title: China’s CXMT Claims Memory Breakthrough, Challenging Samsung and SK Hynix
hook_text: China's CXMT reveals a new memory design.
script:
China's CXMT just revealed a new memory architecture design.
This layout uses a four F-squared, or 4F2, cell structure.
It shrinks the DRAM cell size compared to standard 6F2 designs.
This breakthrough aims to increase density for high-performance memory.
Industry leaders Samsung and SK Hynix currently dominate the HBM market.
CXMT is working to close this gap despite existing trade sanctions.
Will this design make Chinese chips more competitive?

editor.one_line: Weak visuals and generic stock footage undermine a technically interesting news story.
script_fixes: LINE 1: Change to 'China's CXMT has achieved a major DRAM manufacturing milestone.'
LINE 5: Remove 'Industry leaders' to avoid filler; start with 'Samsung and SK Hynix currently dominate...'
LINE 7: Make the question more specific: 'Can 4F2 architecture help CXMT bypass current export restrictions?'
visual_notes: line 1: Stock footage of people in suits is irrelevant and unprofessional for a tech news account.
line 2: Visuals are static text cards; needs a diagram or technical schematic of the 4F2 structure
line 4: Visuals are repetitive; the same 'Higher memory density' card is held for too long.
line 5: Visuals are just text; should show logos of Samsung and SK Hynix side-by-side.
line 6: Using a screenshot of the article is lazy; use a map or trade sanction icon.
